question: What was the average daily number of visitors to Tokyo Disney Resort (Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea combined) in September 2026?

target.what: Average daily number of visitors (park admissions/visits, not unique people) to Tokyo Disney Resort, i.e. Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea combined, during September 2026, expressed as total monthly admissions divided by the number of days in September 2026 (30).
target.publisher: No official daily/monthly visitor series is published by Oriental Land Co. (operator); attendance is disclosed only in aggregate annual/fiscal figures and occasional press reports. Any monthly figure would be an estimate or third-party (e.g. TEA/AECOM Themed Entertainment Association) reconstruction
target.cadence: Annual (fiscal year, April–March) attendance disclosures by Oriental Land; TEA/AECOM Theme Index annual; no official monthly or daily cadence.
target.caveats: Working interpretation: total park admissions (visits) across both gates in September 2026 divided by 30 days. assumptions.name: September 2026 attendance growth vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: Q1 FY2026 attendance was +7% y/y (p51) with monthly detail +4/+13/+3 (p52–p54); the maihama-lab Jan–Jun 2026 multipliers of ~1.20–1.21 (p31/p32) are a different index and are not directly comparable. September is a low month with a mid-month Halloween start, so a modest positive growth is plausible; the range spans flat to strong growth.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale a September 2025 attendance level to September 2026; assumes no major shock (typhoon closure, price change) in September 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Oriental Land Q2 FY2026 disclosure showing September 2026 attendance flat or declining y/y, or a major closure event.

assumptions.name: September share of annual attendance
assumptions.rationale: September is the second-lowest month by congestion index (p19/p20: land 39, sea 47 vs annual peak 75/79 in November, p25/p26). A share below 1/12 (0.083) is implied; the range reflects uncertainty in how congestion maps to attendance.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert an annual attendance total into a September monthly total; assumes the congestion-index ranking is a reasonable proxy for the attendance seasonal profile.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published monthly attendance split showing September materially above or below this range.

assumptions.name: September 2026 congestion-to-attendance calibration factor
assumptions.rationale: The aggregator's mean congestion of 75% (p95) is a percent-of-capacity measure; converting it to realised attendance requires a capacity and a utilisation bridge. This factor represents the ratio of realised daily attendance to (mean congestion × combined capacity), calibrated so that the implied daily average is consistent with the FY2025 annual average of ~75k/day (p17) and the pre-COVID ~87–89k/day (p65/p66).
assumptions.applies_when: Used only in the capacity-utilisation route; assumes combined capacity is roughly the pre-COVID admission-restriction thresholds (p35–p38) and that the aggregator's percent scale is linear in attendance.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the aggregator's congestion score is not proportional to attendance, or a published September 2026 daily attendance figure.

assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 attendance grows modestly relative to September 2025, consistent with Q1 momentum but not extrapolating the +7% quarter.
assumptions.falsified_by: Oriental Land Q2 FY2026 disclosure showing September 2026 attendance flat or declining, or a major closure/typhoon.

methods.label: m1

p17.role: FY2025 (Apr 2025–Mar 2026) combined annual admissions, both parks

methods.rationale: Annual FY2025 admissions (p17) times a September seasonal share (a1) divided by 30 days. Uses the most reliable annual anchor; the September share is the dominant uncertainty, informed by congestion indices (p19/p20, p27/p28) showing September as a low month. Does not adjust for 2026 y/y growth, so it is a conservative level estimate.

methods.label: m2

a3.role: September 2025 daily average admissions, both parks

a2.role: September 2026 vs September 2025 attendance change factor

methods.rationale: September 2025 daily average (a3) scaled by the 2026 y/y change factor (a2). Anchors on the prior-year same-month level and applies the Q1 FY2026 momentum (+7%, p51) tempered by the September 2025 base (-2%, p102) and the 25th-anniversary event (p124). Shares the annual-attendance dependency with m1 but uses a different seasonal bridge.
methods.error: formula_mc must use at least one kept observed data point (a formula made only of assumptions is rejected)

methods.label: m3

p17.role: FY2025 combined annual admissions, both parks

methods.rationale: Alternative formulation: annual daily average (p17/365) times the September-to-annual-average ratio implied by a1 (September share × 365/30). Algebraically equivalent to m1 but expresses the seasonal uplift explicitly; included to test sensitivity to the share parameterization. Shares inputs with m1, so not independent confirmation.

kept.name: September share of annual admissions
kept.rationale: September is a low month (Halloween only in the second half; school term). Congestion indices (p19/p20, p27/p28) put September near the annual low, well below 1/12=0.083. A share around 0.07 of annual admissions is consistent with a low-month position; range spans 0.06–0.086.
kept.applies_when: Annual admissions are roughly evenly distributed with September as a below-average month, as the congestion indices indicate.
kept.falsified_by: A published monthly split showing September materially above ~8.6% or below ~6% of annual admissions.

kept.name: September 2026 y/y attendance change factor
kept.rationale: Q1 FY2026 attendance was +7% y/y (p51) but Q2 FY2025 September was -2% y/y (p102); the 25th-anniversary event (p124) and strong Q1 momentum suggest modest positive growth, tempered by the September 2025 base and the conflicting congestion signals (p29/p30 vs p95). Centered near +2% with wide range.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 attendance grows modestly relative to September 2025, consistent with Q1 momentum but not extrapolating the +7% quarter.
kept.falsified_by: Oriental Land Q2 FY2026 disclosure showing September 2026 attendance flat or declining, or a major closure/typhoon.

kept.name: September 2025 daily average admissions (both parks)
kept.rationale: FY2025 annual 27.53M (p17) over 365 days ≈ 75,400/day average; September is a low month, so daily average is below the annual mean. ~66,000/day is a plausible low-month level, bracketed by pre-COVID ~87–89k (p65/p66) and current lower attendance.
kept.applies_when: September 2025 daily average sits below the FY2025 annual daily mean, consistent with September being a low month.
kept.falsified_by: A published September 2025 monthly total or daily average outside the 55k–78k range.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
